list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: llm-server scrapes the model server directly; llm-server-via-proxy scrapes it through monitor/serve.py and, by default, contributes only the monitor's own llm_monitor_* series — so leaving both selected does not double-count model-server series. If you change prometheus.yml so both carry the server's metrics, pick exactly one job here.

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance
list.description: Every scraped target. An empty result (no data yet) still means All = .* rather than an errored panel.

list.name: model
list.label: Model
list.description: Taken from the server's own model / model_name label where it has one. A server that labels nothing returns no values, All (=.*) is then the only option, and every panel still renders (grouped under 'unknown').

panels.title: Decode tok/s
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total|llamacpp:predicted_tokens_total"}[$__rate_interval]))

The windowed rate over the counter — the correct version of the server's own llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds gauge, which is an average since the last scrape and restarts with the process.

Rate windows are $__rate_interval (at least 4 scrape intervals, so 15s scrapes get ~1m): short enough to see a collapse, long enough that a single dropped scrape is not a cliff. Counter resets and restarts are handled by rate(); gaps are drawn as gaps, never as 0.

panels.title: Prompt tok/s
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(rate({__name__=~"llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total|vllm:prompt_tokens_total"}[$__rate_interval]))

Prefill throughput. llama.cpp counts only the prompt tokens that MISSED the prompt cache in this counter, which is why the cache panel computes cached / (processed + cached) rather than cached / processed.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: PromQL: sum(llamacpp:requests_processing) and sum(llamacpp:requests_deferred) — instant gauges, deliberately no rate(). deferred > 0 means the slot/KV budget is full and arrivals are waiting.

panels.title: KV cache used
panels.description: PromQL: max(llamacpp:kv_cache_usage_ratio) — a 0..1 ratio shown as a percentage. The same series the LLMKVCachePressure alerts read, so this tile and the alerts can never disagree.

panels.title: Throughput — decode vs prompt (this is the 7-day panel)
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(rate(<tokens_total>[$__rate_interval])) in both directions, plus sum(llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds) overlaid — the server's own 'average since the last scrape' figure, left in on purpose while the bespoke page is being retired: where the two disagree, rate() is the one that survives a restart or a counter reset, so drop the overlay once you stop reading it.

The old page could only show ~60 samples held in one browser tab; this panel answers 'what was decode throughput at 03:00' for as long as retention allows (PROMETHEUS_RETENTION_TIME).

Rate windows are $__rate_interval (at least 4 scrape intervals, so 15s scrapes get ~1m): short enough to see a collapse, long enough that a single dropped scrape is not a cliff. Counter resets and restarts are handled by rate(); gaps are drawn as gaps, never as 0.

panels.title: Per-model decode tok/s
panels.description:
PromQL: sum by (model) (label_replace(label_replace(rate(<tokens_total>[$__rate_interval]), "model", "$1", "model_name", "(.*)"), "model", "unknown", "model", "^$"))

The two label_replace calls map llama.cpp (a ``model`` label from file_sd, or none) and vLLM (``model_name``) onto one name, and turn 'no model label at all' into the literal 'unknown' so the legend is never blank. $model filters it; All (=.*) matches the empty label too.

panels.title: Requests / s and structured share
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(rate({__name__=~"halogen:requests_total|llamacpp:requests_total"}[$__rate_interval])), and halogen:structured_requests_total / clamp_min(halogen:requests_total, 1).

clamp_min keeps a restart's 0/0 from rendering NaN. halogen:* only exists on the halogen front door; on a plain llama.cpp server the second series is absent rather than wrong.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Lifetime tok/s — what the old tile actually showed
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total) / clamp_min(sum(llamacpp:tokens_predicted_seconds_total), 1)

This is the arithmetic the bespoke page did in JavaScript: two raw counters, no window, no reset handling. Kept deliberately, as a floor to sanity-check the windowed rates against — it cannot tell you WHEN anything was slow, which is what the panels above are for.

panels.title: Latency histograms on this server?
panels.description:
PromQL: count({__name__=~"..._bucket" for TTFT / TPOT / end-to-end}) or vector(0).

Read this panel first: 0 means this build answers /metrics with averages only (several llama.cpp builds do), so the quantile panels below have nothing to compute and will say No data — that is a server capability, not a monitoring outage. Use the lifetime panel in the Overview row and the raw exposition on the monitor page in that case.

panels.title: Time to first token (TTFT)
panels.description:
PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.5|0.9|0.99, sum by (le) (rate({__name__=~"llama:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|llamacpp:time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket|vllm:request_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket"}[$__rate_interval])))

The panel the old page could not render at all: p99 TTFT over a week. sum by (le) is required — quantiles must never be taken per-label-set and averaged afterwards.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Time per output token (TPOT)
panels.description:
PromQL: histogram_quantile over llama:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket (and the llamacpp: spelling) with sum by (le).

This is decode latency per token: multiply by the decode rate to see what a batch is really paying. If it rises while decode tok/s falls, it is queueing or KV pressure, not the model.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: End-to-end response time
panels.description:
PromQL: histogram_quantile over llama:end_to_end_response_seconds_bucket (llamacpp: and vllm: spellings) with sum by (le).

TTFT + generation time: what a caller experiences. Compare with TTFT to separate 'slow to start' (prefill, cache misses, queueing) from 'slow to finish' (decode throughput).

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: KV cache usage — was it saturated overnight?
panels.description: PromQL: max by (instance) (llamacpp:kv_cache_usage_ratio), with avg_over_time(...[1h]) as the 'was it full overnight, or just spiky' answer. Bands at 80% (warn) and 90% (critical) match the alert thresholds in alert_thresholds.env. Set the range to 12h/24h: this is the exact question the old page could not answer.

panels.title: KV tokens vs pool size
panels.description:
PromQL: sum(llamacpp:kv_cache_tokens) against max(halogen:kv_pool_positions | halogen:kv_pool_reserved_tokens).

Tokens in the cache versus the pool that was configured: the flat top of the pool line is the ceiling the ratio is measured against, and reserved above used means slots have claimed space they are not using.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Prompt-cache hit ratio
panels.description:
PromQL: rate(halogen:prompt_tokens_cached_total) / clamp_min(rate(llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total) + rate(halogen:prompt_tokens_cached_total), 1)

Moved out of JavaScript and into PromQL, so it is now windowed, counter-reset-safe and comparable across restarts. The + cached in the denominator is llama.cpp's convention: prompt_tokens_total counts only the tokens that missed the cache. clamp_min kills the 0/0 spike a restart leaves behind (the JS version hid it with a divide() guard).

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Prompt-cache hit ratio, per model
panels.description:
PromQL: the same ratio, grouped by model with the label_replace chain described in the Overview row.

Caveat: at token level this is a sum across models only when the server labels its counters per model; llama.cpp does not, so on a single-model server every series lands under 'unknown' and this panel duplicates the one to its left. That is the honest rendering of a server that cannot answer the question.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Draft acceptance ratio
panels.description:
PromQL: rate(halogen:draft_tokens_accepted_total) / clamp_min(rate(halogen:draft_tokens_total), 1)

Speculative-decode acceptance, computed with rate() instead of the ratio of two instantaneous counters the old tile showed. clamp_min is deliberate: without it a restart's 0/0 renders as NaN and the panel goes blank in the worst possible moment.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Drafted vs accepted tokens / s
panels.description:
PromQL: rate(halogen:draft_tokens_total) and rate(halogen:draft_tokens_accepted_total).

The raw pair behind the ratio: drafted collapsing to 0 while decode continues means the draft head stopped contributing (MTP off, or a build change), which the ratio alone cannot distinguish from 'drafting and always wrong'.

No data on this panel means this server never exposed the metric — that is the supported 'this build has no such family' case, not an outage. The raw series list on monitor/serve.py's metrics card is the place to see what a server actually answers.

panels.title: Scrape success (up) per job
panels.description:
PromQL: up — 1 when Prometheus successfully scraped the target on its last attempt. A 0 here with a healthy-looking model server means the monitoring path broke, not the model. The llm-server-via-proxy row is the monitor's own passthrough.

Rate windows are $__rate_interval (at least 4 scrape intervals, so 15s scrapes get ~1m): short enough to see a collapse, long enough that a single dropped scrape is not a cliff. Counter resets and restarts are handled by rate(); gaps are drawn as gaps, never as 0.

panels.title: Monitor scrape health (llm_monitor_*)
panels.description:
PromQL: the proxy's own series, appended by monitor/serve.py to its GET /metrics passthrough. This is what makes 'the monitor is broken' visible as a broken monitor instead of a flat-lined model server: scrape success rate, scrape latency, series count and parse errors, all in PromQL rather than only in the page.

Absent on this panel = nothing is scraping the passthrough (the llm-server-via-proxy job is off or mispointed), which is what LLMMonitorAbsent alerts on.

Rate windows are $__rate_interval (at least 4 scrape intervals, so 15s scrapes get ~1m): short enough to see a collapse, long enough that a single dropped scrape is not a cliff. Counter resets and restarts are handled by rate(); gaps are drawn as gaps, never as 0.

panels.title: Scraped series per target
panels.description: PromQL: scrape_samples_scraped and scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling — Prometheus's own view of how much each target contributes. This is the input to the retention sizing in monitoring/README.md; a jump here is the first sign a server started emitting a new (expensive) family.

panels.title: Scrape duration vs the 5s budget
panels.description: PromQL: scrape_duration_seconds against scrape_timeout_seconds. A model server that takes longer than 5s to answer /metrics is too busy to serve and too busy to be watched, and the scrape_timeout matches serve.py's own 5s upstream cap so the two layers fail the same way.
